transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-30 16:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Connor Li (Redwood SE), Daniel Cruz (Zenith Head of AI), Priya Mehta (Zenith Platform), Omar Khalid (Zenith Security), Sara Lopez (Zenith Product)
Shared artifacts: demo deck (link), sample prompt set (drive/zenith-promptset.csv), benchmark template (drive/zenith-bench.xlsx)

Summary:
Quick product walkthrough of Redwood Console and Optimize features focusing on evaluation / quality monitoring: prompt sets, regression alerts, and traffic-split A/B comparisons. Customer wants to understand how to detect regressions when rolling new prompts/models and how to run canary traffic splits with metric-based rollbacks. Security and on-prem/private deployment constraints discussed briefly.

Topics:
- prompt sets and labelled scoring
- regression alerting (thresholds, MLOps hooks)
- traffic-split / A/B compare in Console
- API vs Console flows and where Optimize suggestions run
- security: SOC2, KMS, VPC options

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, uh who do we have on from Zenith?
[00:08] Daniel (Zenith): Daniel here, hi Maya, and Priya, Omar and Sara are on as well. thanks for doing this.
[00:12] Maya: awesome, i'll do a 3 minute context then Connor will jump into console and run a traffic split example. sound good?
[00:20] Priya (Zenith): yep, we mainly want to see how you detect quality regressions across prompt variations, and can we automate alerts to Slack or PagerDuty. also how the traffic splitting would look for a live canary.
[00:32] Connor (Redwood SE): cool. quick note — we'll be using the Evaluate tab in Console and the Optimize suggestions for batching/quantization recs, but the same flows are available via API if you automating it in your pipelines.
[00:45] Daniel: great. can you also show how we correlate token costs to quality drop? that's a big procurement question for us.
[00:52] Maya: yes we'll show cost breakdown in the per-route analytics, and how alerts can be tied to both metric thresholds and cost anomalies.

[00:58] [01:00] Connor: ok i'm sharing my screen - opening Console - here's the Project for Zenith-demo. first pane is Prompt Sets. we've uploaded sample prompts you sent earlier — oh, note transcription: the file showed up as zenith_promptset.csv, slight header mismatch but works.
[01:20] Connor: so prompt sets lets you create labelled examples and attach evaluators — we support pairwise, exact-match, and custom scoring functions. for insurance claim triage we recommend a mixture of pairwise and a custom rubric for compliance.
[01:35] Priya: when you say custom rubric how is it run? server-side or we need to provide code?
[01:40] Connor: good question. the rubric runs as a lightweight JS lambda inside Redwood Evaluate — it executes on the examples bucket and returns a numeric score. you can run it via API or in-console. it's sandboxed and doesn't access your secrets.
[01:51] Omar (Zenith Security): sandboxed how? we need to know for our security review whether it can call external endpoints.
[01:56] Connor: it cannot call external endpoints. it's containerized with no egress. we also support a policy to run evals in your VPC for private deployments.

[02:10] [02:30] Maya: quick demo of regression alerts - imagine you push a new prompt variant to prod. you set an alert on the median pairwise score dropping below .82 across the prompt set and also a latency p95 above 400ms. if either triggers, the alert posts to Slack and triggers a webhook which can hit your internal deploy system to pause rollout.
[02:50] Sara (Zenith): can that webhook trigger a rollback automatically? we prefer automatic cutovers for high severity.
[02:56] Connor: yep, we have a default playbook: on critical regression -> mark canary as failed, initiate rollback via your CI/CD webhook; for non-critical you can create a ticket instead. these playbooks are editable.

[03:10] [03:30] Daniel: show us the A/B compare UI. we want to run 80/20 split for two model variants and see pairwise comparisons, example-level diffs, and aggregated metrics.
[03:39] Connor: sure — switching to Traffic Splits. here's a live split config page. you pick two routes (route here maps to model+prompt version). set traffic: control 80 / treatment 20, add metrics to log (pairwise_score, toxicity_flag, latency_ms, token_cost). you can also add custom evaluators from your prompt set.
[03:58] Priya: does traffic split handle session affinity for chat conversations? we can't fragment a multi-turn session.
[04:04] Connor: yes we expose session_id routing so conversation stickiness is preserved. for streaming chat we keep the KV cache consistent on the same backend instance when configured for affinity.

[04:18] [04:30] Maya: question from procurement — how do we show cost delta? the console shows per-token bill and estimated monthly delta if treatment becomes default.
[04:39] Daniel: good, put that on the report.

[04:44] [05:00] Connor: now i'll create a mock canary — naming the control v1 and treatment v2-augmented prompt. starting traffic split. you can see live events: tokens served, sample outputs, diffs inline. here's a sample where treatment changed phrasing and pairwise score dropped from 0.87 to 0.74 on a subset. you'll also see 'regression alert pending' in top-right.
[05:25] Sara: those inline diffs look handily useful. are they exportable?
[05:30] Connor: yes export to CSV or JSON; we also attach context (conversation id, input prompt, model config) for triage.

[05:36] [06:00] Omar: from security side, two quick asks — audit logs must be immutable and we need KMS for keys. also full data residency in EU for PII. can Redwood do KMS and EU-only processing?
[06:12] Maya: yes, Private deployment supports customer-managed KMS and region pinning. our hosted API can be region-restricted to EU cloud regions and we provide audit logs with WORM retention options for enterprise. i'll send SOC2 and architecture doc after this call.
[06:26] Omar: thanks. also is there an HSM option?
[06:29] Connor: HSM integrations are supported in Private deployments via the on-prem gateway. we'd need a short architecture workshop for the specifics.

[06:40] [07:00] Daniel: operational question — if we see a regression in production, how granular are you on root-cause? can we see per-prompt, per-customer segment, per-model variant?
[07:10] Connor: yes all of that — the dashboard supports slicing by metadata tags. we recommend tagging by customer_segment and traffic_bucket so comparisons are straightforward. plus you can run pairwise diffs scoped to a subset and the system will compute statistical significance for A/B. note the sig tests are approximate for heavy-tailed distributions; we provide guidance in the runbook.

[07:30] [07:45] Maya: quick aside — Optimize will suggest batching and quantization profiles to reduce token cost for the same quality; that can be used during the canary to see if cost improvements hold.
[07:56] Priya: can Optimize suggestions be applied automatically? we prefer manual approval but automation is nice.
[08:02] Connor: suggestions appear as recommended configs in the Console; you can auto-apply for non-breaking changes or require manual approval for perf/quant changes.

[08:15] [08:30] Daniel: any limitations on the prompt set size for running full evals? we have a million+ examples stored in-house.
[08:36] Connor: for huge corpora we recommend sampling or running evals in your VPC where you can attach compute. Console supports incremental evals and delta monitoring rather than full-sweep every push. we'll work with your infra team to run bulk evals with the benchmark harness.

[08:52] [09:00] Maya: let's walk through a failure scenario — treatment triggers pairwise < .8 and p95 > 500ms. that'll trigger critical severity. do you want me to flip to the playbook for that?
[09:10] Sara: yes please. show what users see.
[09:14] Connor: showing playbook — severity mapping, Slack channels, CI/CD rollback webhook. here's the alert detail page with example outputs flagged as low score. you can click open to create a triage ticket, assign to owner, and attach the failing prompt set slice.

[09:32] [09:45] Priya: can we forward alerts to PagerDuty with payload containing conversation id and a short snippet?
[09:50] Connor: yep payload is customizable; we have templates for PD, Slack and Webhook generic. we can include sanitized snippets to avoid PII leakage.

[09:58] [10:30] Daniel: what about drift detection over time — not just canary failures but slow degradation?
[10:36] Connor: we do baseline drift detection — rolling window distributions for scores and embeddings drift. if you enable an embeddings-based centroid monitor, it will surface semantic drift and you can tie it to retrain pipelines.

[10:55] [11:00] Maya: time check — 45 minutes left. Connor can run the benchmark script next if you want to see a small live run, or we can move to Q&A. which do you prefer?
[11:08] Daniel: benchmark run would be great, short 10 minute run is fine.

[11:15] [11:30] Connor: ok kicking off a 10m synthetic benchmark: 1000 requests across both variants, capturing latency, tokens, and pairwise score. note this is synthetic and not your real traffic.
[11:42] Connor: live feed shows latency p95 control 320ms treatment 410ms, pairwise mean ctrl 0.86 treat 0.78, cost delta +12%. system marked treatment as degraded and queued alert.
[12:05] Priya: that mirrors the earlier sample. so we'd run 48h with real traffic for a robust signal?
[12:10] Connor: yes 48-72h recommended for stable metrics. our standard pilot template uses 7 days for full statistical confidence but 48h is a pragmatic starting point.

[12:22] [12:45] Omar: security follow-up — can we have the logs forwarded to our SIEM? Splunk?
[12:50] Connor: yes via syslog or S3 export with lifecycle rules. we support streaming to Splunk Enterprise and cloud collectors.

[13:00] [13:20] Daniel: procurement note — we may want a dedicated pool rather than hosted to meet latency SLOs and isolation. how does that change onboarding?
[13:28] Maya: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity and stronger SLAs. onboarding involves a commit and capacity sizing call; we can start with a small reserved pool for pilot and scale up if needed.

[13:40] [14:00] Sara: client-side question — our call center main use-case has heavy multi-turn. session affinity and KV cache concerns aside, can Redwood pre-warm caches for known customers to reduce p95?
[14:10] Connor: yes we have pre-warm hooks and warm-start via KV cache seeding. Optimize can also recommend pre-batching windows for predictable spikes.

[14:25] [14:45] Daniel: any add-ons for longer retention of eval artifacts? we need 1 year for audits.
[14:50] Maya: enterprise retention add-on supports 1+ years of eval records with export and WORM storage.

[15:05] [15:30] Priya: small nit — sometimes the console model names are different from what our infra calls them; will there be a canonical mapping?
[15:36] Connor: yes we recommend using route aliases that map to your internal identifiers; aliases are sticky across deployments and exposed in audit logs.

[15:50] [16:30] Maya: circling back to next steps — we'll share SOC2, private deployment architecture, and a benchmark script. Connor will run a 48h 80/20 test on a Redwood dev pool and share results. Zenith to provide their prompt set and baseline numbers.

[16:45] [17:00] Daniel: timeline — if everything looks good we'll kick a pilot in mid-July, is that realistic?
[17:06] Maya: yes sounds reasonable. we'll follow up with dates in the next 48 hours.

[17:14] [17:30] Sara: thanks — this was very helpful.
[17:34] Maya: great thanks everyone, we'll send the docs. Connor anything else?
[17:38] Connor: i'll drop the benchmark harness link in the follow-up, and a sample webhook payload for your security team to review.
[17:46] [17:55] Daniel: nice, look forward to it.

Crosstalk and small frags later in the call; closing at 16:54 UTC.

Notes on transcript: transcription contains occasional name mismatches and minor punctuation errors consistent with automated transcription. We preserved conversational hesitations, overlapping talk lines, and some mis-transcribed product names (e.g., 'Redwood Optima' -> meant Redwood Optimize).

End of transcript.
